title: Supplier continuity scenarios and prospect recon for model-landscape resilience
creator: Jordan Kim
description: Objective: Produce an operational playbook and prioritized prospect list that the go-to-market and ops teams can use when a primary model supplier exhibits supply instability (latency spikes, capacity rationing, or license changes). This ticket covers competitive mapping, gap scoring, and three continuity scenarios (fast failover, graceful degradation, and negotiated temporary SLA). Deliverables: 1) A ranked candidate list of replacement models with cost/latency delta estimates and compatibility notes; 2) A set of trigger thresholds (latency/cost/availability) and automated alert routes to start playbook execution; 3) A one-page runbook for sales/support with sample messaging and rollback criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Ranked list of >=6 candidate model variants (open and licensed) with token-cost and median P95 latency estimates per region
Compatibility matrix for top-3 candidates showing required quantization/ops-change effort in person-days
Three scenario runbooks (fast failover, graceful degradation, negotiated SLA) with step-by-step ops tasks and owner assignments
Automated threshold spec (metrics + alerts) checked in Console dashboards and Metabase queries linked
Stakeholder review signoff from Sales, Solutions Eng, and Platform Reliability

notes: Trade-offs: fast failover favors smaller model size + quantized variants (lower latency, higher risk of quality regressions). Graceful degradation uses caching and prefix trimming to preserve model quality at cost of slower throughput improvements.
Decision anchor: prioritize models with identical tokenization and transformer block structure where possible to minimize model conversion work.
Risk: Some enterprise customers have contractual clauses disallowing certain open model forks; coordinate with Account teams before automated failovers are enabled for those accounts.
Ops note: require a rollback window and canary on 10% of traffic before full switchover. Include automatic metric hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping during transient provider instability.
